text:
ash: FYI nodepool canary failing in eu-west-1 — GPU nodes are stuck PendingIP for ~20m after yesterday's CNI chart rollout via GitOps.
leo: saw the alert. `kubectl describe` shows 'failed to allocate IP' and aws-node logs 'ENI capacity exhausted' on new pods.
maria: exact error from kubelet: `failed to set up network for sandbox: failed to allocate IP: subnet free IPs: 0` — reproducible on 2/3 new g4dn nodes.
ash: digging — terraform created the nodegroup fine but the Helm chart we rolled changed ipam defaults. I think `eniMaxPods` got lowered from 58 -> 20 in the new chart (v1.14.2). that plus small subnet in the AZ = immediate exhaustion.
kevin: @ash can you paste the helm values you saw? I remember a PR touched defaults last week (PR 4762).
ash: snippet from the applied values:
```yaml
aws-cni:
  eniMaxPods: 20
  ipam:
    mode: host-local
```
leo: ugh. Rolling back to v1.13.9 restores eniMaxPods=58. But GitOps already applied the bad chart to 5 clusters. We should pause sync and revert in repo before more canaries roll.
maria: pausing ArgoCD sync for EU clusters now: `argocd app set redwood-cni-eu --sync-policy none` — done.
sre-bot: incident INC-2026-045 created: "GPU canary IP exhaustion (eu-west-1)" — paging oncall.
kevin: immediate mitigations: 1) revert chart to v1.13.9 (PR to repo), 2) temporarily increase nodegroup max to 8 so ASG can bring extra nodes, 3) open ENI quota ticket (longer lead time).
ash: created PR 5751 to pin chart to v1.13.9 and added a helm-values unit test to catch low eniMaxPods. https://git.company/infra/PR/5751
leo: note on cost: scaling GPUs to 8 for the emergency will spike monthly spend ~+$8k for the cluster if sustained. finance-ops, are we OK for a temporary emergency bump?
finance-ops: temporary spike approved for incident remediation. please revert asap and send spend estimate after fix.
maria: rollout plan: pause GitOps (done), merge revert PR, manual sync on eu clusters, run `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep PendingIP` and target 0 failures; if still stuck, run `terraform apply -var 'ng_max=8' -target=module.nodegroup.eu-west-1` to scale up nodes.
ash: running terraform scale now: `terraform apply -var 'ng_max=8' -target=module.nodegroup.eu-west-1` — will post plan + apply output.
leo: afterwards we should add a CI gate: fail chart lints if `eniMaxPods < 32` for any chart targeting gpu nodegroups, and add a preflight that checks subnet free IPs before a canary.
kevin: agree. also long-term: switch ipam to prefix mode or increase subnet CIDRs for gpu AZs so ENI limits don't bite us again. once canary stable we'll revert nodegroup max and re-enable GitOps.
ash: update: terraform plan applied, ASG scaling to 8 in progress. will follow up with pod state in 10m. :thumbsup:
